about: Zenkai Rules Z1 intent examples: tests/host_support.py::assert_no_concurrent_darktable, a Z5 detector against two darktable launches sharing a plugin config, library.db or bridge spool. Called explicitly by each host test as its own first action (never from PluginInstall.install(), so a non-host unit test of PluginInstall never depends on the real host's live spool). Two independent checks: a second darktable process (pgrep -x darktable, injected here via `darktable_running` rather than mocking subprocess itself -- the real file-scanning half of the guard is exercised unmocked, against a real temp cache dir) and a bridge request/response file in the spool younger than a staleness window (darktable_mcp/bridge/client.py's request-<id>.json/response-<id>.json pair, default 300s; an older file is an orphan the bridge's own sweep would eventually collect, not evidence of a call in flight; the heartbeat file and cli-config/ directory are normal residents of a live spool per an `ls` of ~/.cache/darktable-mcp and must NOT trip the guard either way). File ages are set with os.utime, never a real sleep. Two oracles per example (Z2): whether the call raised at all, and (when it does) that the message names the actual cause, not a generic refusal -- a guard that raises for the wrong reason would still pass a raises-only check.
subject: tests/host_support.py::assert_no_concurrent_darktable

examples.source: incident inc_f9c5e8f5's actual root cause: a second darktable process already running. The file-spool side is irrelevant here and must not need to fail too for this to refuse.

the spool-side half of the incident: a request file still on disk means some darktable's Lua worker has not answered it yet -- another session may be mid-call. No darktable process check alone would have caught this if pgrep raced the process exiting.
the other half of one request/response pair: an unread response file is just as much evidence of an in-flight (or racing) call as the request file.

a live spool always has a heartbeat file and a cli-config/ directory (confirmed by ls ~/.cache/darktable-mcp on this host) -- the guard must not treat every non-empty cache dir as contaminated, only an actual pending request/response pair.
the ordinary case every host test needs to keep passing: nothing running, nothing pending.

an orphaned late response to a request the client already gave up on (normal bridge behaviour, observed after a real rerun: pgrep was empty yet a response file from over an hour earlier still sat in the spool). Once no darktable is running, an old file cannot be evidence of a call in flight, so it must not block a later host test.
the staleness window must not swallow the real case: a request file written just now is still evidence of a call in flight and must refuse.
